translation_notes: The two literal SPARQL strings passed to backend.update / backend.query become s{ } islands (an INSERT DATA and a CONSTRUCT). The receiver is the project's InMemoryBackend, not a graph, and its methods forward the argument to rdflib's ConjunctiveGraph.update/query: the island is 'handed to rdflib', so no .execute() and no call suffix. Both queries use full IRIs and no prefix, so no @prefix is needed.
Context shim djangordf_shim.py: the InMemoryBackend of djangordf/backends/memory.py (the `backend` fixture of the source tests), reduced to the methods the region uses; the driver builds it.

The test is an assertion only: the driver shows it through the return/raise of seven backends (empty, same triple already there, other object, other subject, named graph, an update that does nothing, a query that returns an empty graph). A mutant inserting "w" instead of "v" fails the check (verified).
No gain nor loss in size: the island swaps a string for validation at transpile time.
optimization_notes: optimized.py: the update call on one line, the CONSTRUCT result inlined into the assert, and the CONSTRUCT written in its short form CONSTRUCT WHERE { ?s ?p ?o }.
optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: the same two queries as s{ } islands handed to the backend.

The island is kept although the token ratio puts it above the Python: the query is the same SPARQL text on both sides, one string token in optimized.py and tokenised in the island; counted alike (tokens_embedded) the island is not longer.
Almost nothing to compress: a three-statement test. No exception to the symmetry.
header_optimization_notes: No header import on either side: the two files are copies of the optimized ones.
